messages:
drew (product): Quick proposal: "adaptive fallback ladder" for reserved pools. Idea: deterministic ordering of fallback lanes when burst credits exhausted so customers get predictable degradation, and sales can promise a clear fallback. Thoughts?

sam (eng-runtime): +1. We need a deterministic priority ladder and an obvious preemption policy. otherwise scheduler heuristics will make customer experience inconsistent.

priya (eng-sre): Agree. Must include emergency drain, synthetic checks, and automatic region disable if ladder causes >0.5% p99 regressions. Also define what counts as a "fallback failure."

rachel (sales): Customers want one sentence guarantees. Proposed consumer-friendly wording: "If your reserved band is exhausted we will try fallback lanes in order; if lane X is used you may see degraded latency but we will surface that in console and billing." Need examples.

lee (data): I'll provide historical heatmap to estimate how often each ladder rung will be hit for typical tenant shapes. helps define default ladder for small/medium/large pools.

sam (eng-runtime): suggested ladder (config sketch):
```
fallback_ladder:
  - name: regional_warm_spare
    priority: 0
    preemptible: false
  - name: pool_burst_band
    priority: 1
    preemptible: true
  - name: spot_backfill
    priority: 2
    preemptible: true
    cold_start_seconds: 45
  - name: async_queue
    priority: 3
    preemptible: true
    degrade_to: "batch"
```
We can make ordering per-customer and expose opt-in toggles.

priya (eng-sre): For each rung we need SLO impact statements. e.g. regional_warm_spare: p95 = baseline + 5ms, spot_backfill: best-effort (cold start ~45s). async_queue: not real-time. Also monitoring tags to mark requests served via rung X.

drew (product): Product UX: pool settings should let customers choose ladder template (predictable / cost-conscious / latency-first). Default to predictable. Also show "estimated hit probability" per rung in console (lee to supply numbers).

rachel (sales): For contracts, we'll offer an "aggressive fallback" opt-in SKU that enables spot_backfill and charges a backfill fee. Conservative SKU will only use regional_warm_spare + burst_band. Need sample contract language.

lee (data): I'll run the 90-day sim and return hit probabilities and expected extra cost for aggressive mode.

sam (eng-runtime): implementation notes: add per-request rung header, ledger changes for burst_band accounting, and scheduler extension for rung ordering. Estimate: 3 sprints eng-runtime + 1 sprint infra for spot telemetry.

priya (eng-sre): launch gating checklist:
- telemetry: requests_by_rung, ladder_hit_rate, p50/p95/p99 by rung, cold_start_count
- synthetic tests: trigger ladder and verify routing and runbook steps; chaos test where regional_warm_spare is taken away
- pilot: 4 tenants (mix of chat and long-context) for 21 days
- rollback: auto-toggle ladder to conservative for region if ladder_hit_rate causes >0.5% p99 regressions for 4h
- ops runbook: page owners, steps to revoke aggressive fallback per-tenant, and how to quarantine noisy tenant

drew (product): owner list & timeline: sam prototype in 3 weeks, lee deliver sim in 10 days, priya produce SLOs and runbook in 2 weeks, rachel to draft customer messaging and contract wording in 2 weeks. Pilot start target: 6 weeks.

ops-bot: RFC draft created at https://redwood.internal/rfcs/adaptive-fallback-ladder (access: product, eng-runtime, eng-sre, data, sales).

drew (product): thanks all. final ask: make default ladder explicit in RFC and include two pre-made templates (latency-first, cost-first). i'll collate and post checklist Monday. :white_check_mark:

sam (eng-runtime): ack, starting ticket.
